title: India's services sector just hit a 4-month high - while costs hit a 6-year low. November 9, 2026.
excerpt: From a state carved out 26 years ago today, to a Kerala-born mayor-elect of Los Angeles, to a services sector growing faster and cheaper at once, to a Bihar entrepreneur whose lockdown improvisation now supports 25 families - November 9's four stories are about things built once and still paying off.
bodyHtml:
Every story today traces back to a single founding decision - a state born of a 2000 reorganisation, a Kerala upbringing that led to a mayor's office, a services sector whose cost discipline finally caught up with its growth, and an ice cream brand built out of lockdown necessity.

On this day, India got its 27th state - and it took seven more years to get its own name back

Uttarakhand was carved out of Uttar Pradesh on November 9, 2000, capping decades of a grassroots hill-state movement. First named Uttaranchal, it reclaimed its historic name on January 1, 2007.

She was born in Kerala. On November 3, 2026, she was elected the first South Asian woman to lead Los Angeles

Nithya Raman, born in Kerala in 1981, was elected Mayor-elect of Los Angeles, defeating incumbent Karen Bass. She studied at Harvard and MIT before entering LA politics - and her win means both Los Angeles and New York are now led by Indian-origin mayors.

India's services sector just hit a 4-month high - while costs hit a 6-year low

The HSBC India Services PMI rose to 55.8 in October 2026, a four-month high. Input cost inflation for services firms eased to its lowest level in six years - faster growth without rising costs.

She started making ice cream at home during the 2020 lockdown. By 2026, her business crossed Rs 30 lakh a year

Geeta Devi, of Hathsar village in Sheohar district, Bihar, turned a lockdown improvisation into Sagar Ice Cream - a business now supporting roughly 20-25 families through 18 local vendors.

Four stories, one pattern: a state, a career, an economy and a business, each built on a single decision years ago that's still paying dividends today.
